claim: Practically all studies of gene expression in humans to date have been performed in a relatively small number of adult tissues.
source: Practically all studies of gene expression in humans to date have been performed in a relatively small number of adult tissues.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field presented in the abstract without specific data or citations in this sentence.

claim: Gene regulation is highly dynamic and context-dependent.
source: Gene regulation is highly dynamic and context-dependent.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding presented in the abstract.

claim: Mutations that affect developmental processes may be of particular relevance to complex traits.
source: In particular, we need to characterize gene expression in early development cell types, as mutations that affect developmental processes may be of particular relevance to complex traits.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential relevance of developmental mutations to complex traits.

claim: Embryoid bodies (EBs) are organoids that contain a multitude of cell types in dynamic states.
source: To address this challenge, we propose to use embryoid bodies (EBs), which are organoids that contain a multitude of cell types in dynamic states.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about EBs based on established knowledge.

claim: EBs provide a system in which one can study dynamic regulatory processes at an unprecedentedly high resolution.
source: EBs provide a system in which one can study dynamic regulatory processes at an unprecedentedly high resolution.
evidence: This is a claim about the capabilities of the EB system based on inference from its properties.

claim: Many GWAS-identified genetic variants associated with human traits and diseases are located in noncoding regions of the genome and are putatively regulatory in function.
source: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified thousands of genetic variants associated with human traits and diseases, many of which are located in noncoding regions of the genome and are putatively regulatory in function (Albert and Kruglyak, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Albert and Kruglyak, 2015.

claim: To understand regulatory and functional effects of trait-associated variants, it is necessary to perform molecular assays in the relevant cell types at the relevant stages of development.
source: To understand regulatory and functional effects of trait-associated variants, it is necessary to perform molecular assays in the relevant cell types at the relevant stages of development, and potentially to also model different environmental exposures (Umans et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Umans et al., 2020.

claim: Most efforts to identify eQTLs have relied on adult tissue samples collected at a single time point.
source: However, most efforts to identify genetic variants that regulate gene expression (expression quantitative trait loci, or eQTLs) have relied on adult tissue samples collected at a single time point.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field based on established knowledge.

claim: GTEx efforts have mapped millions of static, steady-state eQTLs across dozens of tissues and cell types.
source: While such efforts have mapped millions of static, steady-state eQTLs across dozens of tissues and cell types (GTEx Consortium, 2020), most disease-associated variants were not found to also be classified as eQTLs (Yao et al., 2020; Aguet et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to GTEx Consortium, 2020.

claim: Most disease-associated variants were not found to also be classified as eQTLs.
source: While such efforts have mapped millions of static, steady-state eQTLs across dozens of tissues and cell types (GTEx Consortium, 2020), most disease-associated variants were not found to also be classified as eQTLs (Yao et al., 2020; Aguet et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yao et al., 2020 and Aguet et al., 2017.

claim: Dynamic and variable regulatory genetic effects may underlie the mechanisms for many unexplained phenotypic associations.
source: It is possible that dynamic and variable regulatory genetic effects, including those that are specific to a given cell type, time point, or environment, may underlie the mechanisms for many unexplained phenotypic associations.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms.

claim: Recent efforts to characterize gene regulatory dynamics in human iPSCs and their derived cell types have identified dynamic eQTLs that are associated with disease risk.
source: For example, recent efforts to characterize gene regulatory dynamics in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and their derived cell types have identified dynamic eQTLs that are associated with disease risk, supporting the intuitive notion that changes in gene regulation during development may play a role in shaping human adult phenotypes, including disease (Strober et al., 2019; Cuomo et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Strober et al., 2019 and Cuomo et al., 2020.

claim: The number of cell types that can be obtained from iPSCs using directed differentiation protocols is quite modest.
source: Still, iPSCs are limited in their potential for identifying dynamic regulatory effects. The number of cell types that can be obtained from iPSCs using directed differentiation protocols is quite modest, and time-course experiments, although useful for studying gene regulation at discrete points along a continuum, are inefficient, expensive, and laborious to perform.
evidence: This is a statement based on knowledge of current iPSC differentiation capabilities.

claim: Time-course experiments are inefficient, expensive, and laborious to perform.
source: Still, iPSCs are limited in their potential for identifying dynamic regulatory effects. The number of cell types that can be obtained from iPSCs using directed differentiation protocols is quite modest, and time-course experiments, although useful for studying gene regulation at discrete points along a continuum, are inefficient, expensive, and laborious to perform.
evidence: This is a statement based on knowledge of experimental practices.

claim: Embryoid bodies are three-dimensional aggregates of spontaneously and asynchronously differentiating cells.
source: To do this, we used iPSCs to form embryoid bodies (EBs), which are three-dimensional aggregates of spontaneously and asynchronously differentiating cells.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about EBs based on established knowledge.

claim: EB formation has been used to verify stem cell pluripotency for decades.
source: EB formation has been used to verify stem cell pluripotency for decades; yet, until recently, the complexity of EB cellular composition has precluded their use in genomic studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical use of EBs based on established knowledge.

claim: Until recently, the complexity of EB cellular composition has precluded their use in genomic studies.
source: EB formation has been used to verify stem cell pluripotency for decades; yet, until recently, the complexity of EB cellular composition has precluded their use in genomic studies.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of EBs based on established knowledge.

claim: With single-cell RNA-sequencing, it is now possible to characterize the numerous spatially and developmentally distinct cell types within EBs.
source: With single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq), it is now possible to characterize the numerous spatially and developmentally distinct cell types within EBs, including transient cell types that would otherwise be inaccessible.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of scRNA-seq technology based on established knowledge.

claim: Recent scRNA-seq studies of human EB differentiation have revealed the diversity of cell types composing these structures and the transcriptional dynamics governing early fate decisions.
source: Indeed, recent scRNA-seq studies of human EB differentiation have revealed the diversity of cell types composing these structures and the transcriptional dynamics governing early fate decisions (Han et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Han et al., 2018 and Guo et al., 2019.

claim: The only studies that have sequenced EB cells have relied on a small sample of cells from a single individual.
source: To date, however, the only studies that have sequenced EB cells have relied on a small sample of cells from a single individual, leaving a gap in our understanding of technical, biological, and inter-individual variation present in this system (Han et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Han et al., 2018 and Guo et al., 2019.

claim: The study used a batch-controlled study design to generate and sequence EBs from multiple individuals using multiple replicates.
source: To this end, we used a batch-controlled study design to generate and sequence EBs from multiple individuals using multiple replicates.
evidence: This is a statement about the study design used in this work.

claim: The study differentiated EBs from three human iPSC lines (18511, 18858, and 19160) in three replicates.
source: To characterize sources of variation in gene expression in human EBs, we initially differentiated EBs from three human iPSC lines (18511, 18858, and 19160) in three replicates (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design of this study.

claim: The experiment was performed in three batches, where each batch includes one replicate from each of the three individuals.
source: We performed the experiment in three batches, where each batch includes one replicate from each of the three individuals.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design of this study.

claim: EBs differentiate quickly, with cell types representing endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm present after 8 days.
source: EBs differentiate quickly, with cell types representing endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm present after 8 days (Han et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Han et al., 2018.

claim: The study maintained EBs for 3 weeks after formation.
source: In this study, we maintained EBs for 3 weeks after formation, allowing cells to continue to differentiate and mature.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental protocol used in this study.

claim: After 21 days, the study collected scRNA-seq data, targeting equal numbers of cells from each individual in each replicate.
source: After 21 days, we collected scRNA-seq data, targeting equal numbers of cells from each individual in each replicate.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental protocol used in this study.

claim: After filtering and quality control, the study retained high-quality data from a sample of 42,488 cells.
source: After filtering and quality control (Materials and methods), we retained high-quality data from a sample of 42,488 cells (an average of 4721 cells per individual/replicate).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: The study obtained a median of 16,712 UMI counts per cell.
source: For these cells, we obtained a median of 16,712 UMI counts per cell, which allowed us to measure the expression of a median of 4274 genes per cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The study measured the expression of a median of 4274 genes per cell.
source: For these cells, we obtained a median of 16,712 UMI counts per cell, which allowed us to measure the expression of a median of 4274 genes per cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The study integrated data from all cells using Harmony.
source: We integrated data from all cells using Harmony, which anchors the data sets by cell type (Korsunsky et al., 2019)⁠.
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis method used, supported by a citation to Korsunsky et al., 2019.

claim: Individual 18858 had lower differentiation efficiency than the other two lines.
source: After these initial collections, we found that one individual, 18858, had lower differentiation efficiency than the other two lines (Figure 1G, see Differentiation efficiency across individuals).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1G.

claim: The study differentiated EBs in one replicate from each of five additional randomly chosen lines (18856, 18912, 19140, 19159, and 19210).
source: Too assess the robustness of differentiation efficiency and cell type composition among a larger sample of individuals from our YRI iPSC panel, we differentiated EBs in one replicate from each of five additional randomly chosen lines (18856, 18912, 19140, 19159, and 19210).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design of this study.

claim: After filtering and quality control, the study retained an average of 5243 cells per individual in the new set of data.
source: After filtering and quality control, we retained an average of 5243 cells per individual in this new set of data, a median of 5983 UMI counts per cell, and a median of 2775 genes per cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The study found cells expressing markers for endoderm (SOX17, FOXA2), mesoderm (HAND1), and ectoderm (PAX6).
source: We found cells expressing markers for endoderm (SOX17, FOXA2), mesoderm (HAND1), and ectoderm (PAX6), in addition to cells still expressing pluripotency markers (POU5F1, MYC, NANOG).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: The study found cells expressing pluripotency markers (POU5F1, MYC, NANOG).
source: We found cells expressing markers for endoderm (SOX17, FOXA2), mesoderm (HAND1), and ectoderm (PAX6), in addition to cells still expressing pluripotency markers (POU5F1, MYC, NANOG).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: Cells expressing each of these germ layer markers occupied distinct groups in UMAP space.
source: We visualized the data with uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) and observed that cells expressing each of these germ layer markers occupied distinct groups in UMAP space (Figure 1A–D; Becht et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A–D and a citation to Becht et al., 2018.

claim: Every replicate in the experiment includes cells from all three germ layers.
source: Moreover, we found that every replicate in our experiment, regardless of the individual, includes cells from all three germ layers (Figure 1E and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1E and G.

claim: The study used the Louvain algorithm in Seurat to identify groups of cells with similar transcriptomes.
source: For the first approach, we used a standard clustering analysis, the Louvain algorithm in Seurat, to identify groups of cells with similar transcriptomes (Blondel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis method used, supported by a citation to Blondel et al., 2008.

claim: The study repeated clustering analysis across different clustering resolutions (resolution 0.1, 0.5, 0.8, and 1).
source: To avoid making assumptions about the true number of cell types present, we repeated this analysis across different clustering resolutions (resolution 0.1, 0.5, 0.8, and 1).
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis approach used in this study.

claim: The number of clusters identified varied greatly depending on the resolution.
source: As expected, the number of clusters we identified varied greatly depending on the resolution (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1E–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: At resolution 0.1, the study identified seven clusters representing pluripotent cells, early ectoderm, mesoderm, neural crest, endoderm, neurons, and endothelial cells.
source: For example, considering the gene expression data of the seven clusters identified at resolution 0.1, we found that the most significantly upregulated genes in each cluster included known marker genes for pluripotent cells (cluster 0), early ectoderm (cluster 1), mesoderm (cluster 2), neural crest (cluster 3), endoderm (cluster 4), neurons (cluster 5), and endothelial cells (cluster 6) (Figure 1E, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1E and Table 1.

claim: At clustering resolution 1, cluster 19 is characterized by higher expression of hepatocyte marker genes FGB, TTR, and AFP.
source: At higher resolutions, DE analysis between clusters enabled annotation of some more specific cell types; for example, at clustering resolution 1, cluster 19 is characterized by higher expression of hepatocyte marker genes FGB, TTR, and AFP.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: The study integrated EB cells with reference data sets of scRNA-seq data from primary fetal tissues, human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), and hESC-derived EBs.
source: To pursue the second approach, we annotated cells by comparing our gene expression data to available reference sets of scRNA-seq data from primary fetal tissues, human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), and hESC-derived EBs (Cao et al., 2020; Han et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis approach used, supported by citations to Cao et al., 2020 and Han et al., 2020.

claim: Reference hESCs cluster closely with pluripotent EB cells.
source: We observed that reference hESCs cluster closely with pluripotent EB cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: hESC-derived EBs and iPSC-derived EBs tend to occupy the same areas in UMAP space.
source: We also observed that the hESC-derived EBs and our iPSC-derived EBs tend to occupy the same areas in UMAP space, implying high overall similarity in cell type composition despite differing protocols for EB differentiation (and despite the fact that the experiments were performed in different labs).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study, with inference about similarity.

claim: EB cells show overlap with many primary fetal cell types.
source: EB cells also show overlap with many primary fetal cell types (Figure 2B–C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2B–C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: EB cells annotated as neural crest overlap with primary fetal cell types derived from neural crest, such as Schwann cells and enteric nervous system (ENS) glia.
source: For example, EB cells annotated as neural crest based on our gene expression analysis, overlap with primary fetal cell types derived from neural crest, such as Schwann cells and enteric nervous system (ENS) glia (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2B.

claim: EB cells annotated as neurons overlap with fetal neuronal subtypes, including inhibitory neurons, excitatory neurons, granule neurons, ENS neurons, and others.
source: EB cells annotated as neurons based on our gene expression analysis overlap with fetal neuronal subtypes, including inhibitory neurons, excitatory neurons, granule neurons, ENS neurons, and others.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: EB cells show overlap with populations of cells that are rare in the fetal data set, including AFP_ALBpositive cells (hepatic cells), thymic epithelial cells, and lens fibre cells.
source: EB cells also show overlap with populations of cells that are rare in the fetal data set, including AFP_ALBpositive cells (hepatic cells), thymic epithelial cells, and lens fibre cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2C.

claim: The study found EB cells representing 66 of the 77 primary cell types present in the reference fetal data set.
source: Using this approach, we found EB cells representing 66 of the 77 primary cell types present in the reference fetal data set (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: The most common annotation was hESC (80% of EB cells).
source: The most common annotation was hESC (80% of EB cells); this can be partially attributed to the high proportion of pluripotent cells in our EB data set, but also to the fact that the reference fetal data set does not include many early developmental cell types.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study, with inference about the reasons.

claim: Many cells annotated as hESC are likely to represent immature, differentiating cells which are no longer pluripotent but whose transcriptional profiles more closely match hESCs than the more highly differentiated fetal cell types present in the reference data set.
source: Indeed, many cells annotated as hESC here are likely to represent immature, differentiating cells which are no longer pluripotent but whose transcriptional profiles more closely match hESCs than the more highly differentiated fetal cell types present in the reference data set.
evidence: This is an inference about the identity of cells based on the data.

claim: EB data sets may capture transient developmental cell types that are difficult or impossible to study even in fetal primary samples.
source: In this sense, EB data sets may capture transient developmental cell types that are difficult or impossible to study even in fetal primary samples.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of EBs based on the data.

claim: 89% of cells from individual 18858 were assigned to cluster 0, the cluster annotated as pluripotent cells.
source: While EBs from two of the individuals in our study differentiated efficiently across all replicates, we observed that 89% of cells from individual 18858 were assigned to cluster 0, the cluster annotated as pluripotent cells based on differential expression of marker genes (Table 1, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: The EBs from line 18858 do differentiate, producing high quality cells assigned to clusters representing each germ layer.
source: The EBs from this line do differentiate, producing high quality cells assigned to clusters representing each germ layer (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), but these EB have overall markedly lower differentiation efficiency than EBs from individuals 18511 and 19160.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: EBs from additional lines differentiated efficiently, with cell type composition similar to 18511 and 19160.
source: We were reassured to find that EBs from additional lines differentiated efficiently, with cell type composition similar to 18511 and 19160 (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1H.

claim: Poor differentiation efficiency is expected to be rare among the YRI iPSC panel.
source: These results suggest that poor differentiation efficiency is expected to be rare among the YRI iPSC panel.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data from additional lines.

claim: Annotations assigned to cells from the additional lines represented 66/77 fetal cell types.
source: We find that annotations assigned to cells from these additional lines represented 66/77 fetal cell types; this set of annotations included several cell types that were missing in the original three lines, but also excludes several that were seen in the original three lines (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: Most EB cells from the additional lines are annotated as hESC (82% of cells).
source: Again, we observed that most EB cells from the additional lines are annotated as hESC (82% of cells), although many no longer express pluripotency markers and do express markers of various germ layers as we previously observed.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: The study applied topic modeling using fastTopics at a range of topic resolutions, identifying 6, 10, 15, 25, and 30 topics.
source: We applied topic modeling using fastTopics at a range of topic resolutions, identifying 6, 10, 15, 25, and 30 topics in our data.
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis approach used in this study.

claim: In the k = 6 topic analysis, topic 1 is loaded exclusively on cells assigned to Seurat cluster 4 (cluster resolution 0.1) which was previously annotated as endoderm.
source: For example, in the k = 6 topic analysis, topic 1 is loaded exclusively on cells assigned to Seurat cluster 4 (cluster resolution 0.1) which we previously annotated as endoderm (Figures 4A–D–1E, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figures 4A–D–1E and Table 1.

claim: Compared to other topics, topic 1 shows an increase in expression of FN1 and AFP, which are known markers of hepatocytes.
source: Compared to other topics, topic 1 shows an increase in expression of FN1 and AFP, which are known markers of hepatocytes (Figure 4E, Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4E and Table 2.

claim: Topic modeling revealed that endoderm cells exhibit variable grades of membership in topic 1; this gradient captures a temporal continuum of differentiation.
source: Topic modeling revealed that these cells actually exhibit variable grades of membership in topic 1 (in k = 6 topic model); this gradient captures a temporal continuum of differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference about the meaning of the topic modeling results.

claim: Topic 6 from the k = 6 topic analysis is loaded across all Seurat clusters.
source: For example, topic 6 from the k = 6 topic analysis is loaded across all Seurat clusters; compared to all other topics, topic 6 shows increased expression of many ribosomal genes, housekeeping genes (GAPDH), and genes coding for proteins involved in cellular metabolism (LDHA) (Figure 4—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4—figure supplements 1–3.

claim: Topic 6 captures patterns of gene expression associated with cellular processes and functions that are not specific to a particular cell type.
source: This indicates that topic six captures patterns of gene expression associated with cellular processes and functions that are not specific to a particular cell type.
evidence: This is an inference about the meaning of the topic modeling results.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of samples based on the proportion of cells in each Seurat cluster shows that replicate-individual samples cluster first by individual.
source: We began by calculating the proportion of cells that were assigned to each Seurat cluster at resolution 0.1 for each replicate. We then performed hierarchical clustering of the samples based on the proportion of cells in each Seurat cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). Using this approach, replicate-individual samples cluster first by individual, indicating that cell type composition is distinct between individuals and is consistent between replicates of each individual.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: This finding is robust with respect to the number of clusters.
source: We repeated this analysis at a range of cluster resolutions and determined that this finding is robust with respect to the number of clusters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Using topic loadings as a measure of cell type composition, samples generally cluster by individual, but there is also substantial variation between replicates.
source: We also repeated this analysis using topic loadings as a measure of cell type composition. We calculated the loading of each topic on each individual-replicate group and performed hierarchical clustering (Figure 5—figure supplement 2). Again, we found that at varying values of k, samples generally cluster by individual, but using the higher resolution topic-based approach, we also observed substantial variation between replicates (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Individual 18858 always clusters away from the other two lines, due to the consistent and distinct distribution of cell types caused by low differentiation efficiency.
source: Individual 18858 always clusters away from the other two lines, due to the consistent and distinct distribution of cell types caused by low differentiation efficiency.
evidence: This is an inference about the reason for the clustering pattern based on the data.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of pseudobulk expression estimates shows that samples tend to cluster first by cell type (Seurat cluster), then by individual and replicate.
source: Hierarchical clustering of pseudobulk expression estimates of cells from the same Seurat cluster (res. 0.1), replicate, and individual shows that, as might be expected, samples tend to cluster first by cell type (Seurat cluster), then by individual and replicate (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5A.

claim: Replicate and individual explained approximately equal proportions of the variance (each explains a median value of ~5% of variance).
source: We performed variance partitioning using pseudobulk expression levels to estimate the relative contribution of cell type, individual, and replicate to overall patterns of gene expression variation (Figure 5B; Hoffman and Schadt, 2016). We found that replicate and individual explained approximately equal proportions of the variance (each explains a median value of ~5% of variance).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5B and a citation to Hoffman and Schadt, 2016.

claim: Cell type identity explained the largest proportion of variation at all clustering resolutions tested (variance explained median value ~60% at clustering resolution 0.1).
source: Cell type identity explained the largest proportion of variation at all clustering resolutions tested (variance explained median value ~60% at clustering resolution 0.1), although this figure is likely exaggerated since cell type identity is determined by clustering, which will inherently maximize variation between cell types.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study, with a caveat about interpretation.

claim: A median value of approximately 20–30% of variance is explained by residuals.
source: Depending on clustering resolution, a median value of approximately 20–30% of variance is explained by residuals, which can be attributed to noise or other technical variation not specifically modeled (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: At single-cell resolution, replicate explains more variation on average than individuals, with cell type identity continuing to explain more variance than either.
source: We then partitioned the variance in gene expression at single cell resolution (instead of using pseudobulk estimates) and found that replicate explains more variation on average than individuals, with cell type identity continuing to explain more variance than either (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5C.

claim: At single-cell resolution, residuals explain a median value of 93% of the variation.
source: At single-cell resolution, residuals explain a median value of 93% of the variation, which is expected due to the high degree of variance (both biological and technical) in gene expression profiles among individual cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study, with an explanation.

claim: At clustering resolution 0.1, individual contributes more to variation, on average, in clusters 0, 1, 4, and 5, while replicate contributes more to variation in clusters 2, 3, and 6.
source: At clustering resolution 0.1, individual contributes more to variation, on average, in clusters 0, 1, 4, and 5, while replicate contributes more to variation in clusters 2, 3, and 6.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: Clusters 2, 3, and 6 include only a few cells from individual 18858.
source: Notably, clusters 2, 3, and 6 include only a few cells from individual 18858 (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: An experiment consisting of 58 individuals with 3000 cells collected per individual, collected across three replicates (experiment size of 174,000 cells total), would provide 93% power to detect eQTLs with a standardized effect size of 0.6.
source: Assuming a simple linear regression to map eQTLs and a conservative Bonferroni correction for multiple testing (FWER = 0.05, Materials and methods), we estimated that an experiment consisting of 58 individuals with 3000 cells collected per individual, collected across three replicates (experiment size of 174,000 cells total), would provide 93% power to detect eQTLs with a standardized effect size of 0.6.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of a power analysis based on the data.

claim: The study inferred developmental trajectories using PAGA.
source: In order to explore dynamic patterns of gene expression, we inferred developmental trajectories using PAGA (Wolf et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis method used, supported by a citation to Wolf et al., 2019.

claim: Trajectories toward endoderm and mesoderm proceed through cluster 22, which expresses primitive streak marker MIXL1.
source: Trajectories toward endoderm and mesoderm proceed through cluster 22, which expresses primitive streak marker MIXL1, showing recapitulation of developmental trajectories defined during gastrulation (Figure 1F, Figure 7—figure supplement 1, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1F, Figure 7—figure supplement 1, and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Hepatocytes (cluster 19), an endoderm-derived cell type, branch off of the endoderm cluster (cluster 10).
source: Hepatocytes (cluster 19), an endoderm-derived cell type, branch off of the endoderm cluster (cluster 10) (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Neurons (clusters 12, 15), an ectoderm-derived cell type, branch off from the early ectoderm clusters.
source: and neurons (clusters 12, 15), an ectoderm-derived cell type, branch off from the early ectoderm clusters (clusters 2, 3, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 21, 26, and 27) (Figures 7A and 1F, Table 1, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figures 7A, 1F, Table 1, and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The study applied split-GPM to infer dynamic patterns of gene expression within developmental trajectories.
source: Next, we applied split-GPM, an unsupervised probabilistic model, to infer dynamic patterns of gene expression within a particular developmental trajectory, while simultaneously performing clustering of genes and samples.
evidence: This is a statement about the data analysis method used in this study.

claim: The study identified gene modules with distinct dynamic patterns of expression along the trajectories to neurons, hepatocytes, and endothelial cells.
source: We were able to identify gene modules with distinct dynamic patterns of expression along the trajectories to neurons, hepatocytes, and endothelial cells (Figure 7—figure supplements 3–5).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7—figure supplements 3–5.

claim: Gene modules that increase expression through pseudo-time along the differentiation trajectory to hepatocytes are enriched for the hallmark bile acid metabolism and fatty acid metabolism gene sets.
source: For example, we found that gene modules that increase expression through pseudo-time along the differentiation trajectory to hepatocytes, which are the predominant cell type of the liver and are responsible for the production of bile, are enriched for the hallmark bile acid metabolism and fatty acid metabolism gene sets.
evidence: This is a statement about the data obtained in this study.

claim: In the trajectory leading to endothelial cells, a gene module with high expression at intermediate pseudo-time values is enriched for hallmark genes expressed during the epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
source: In the trajectory leading to endothelial cells, which are derived from mesoderm, we found that a gene module with high expression at intermediate pseudo-time values is enriched for hallmark genes expressed during the epithelial-mesenchymal transition, which is essential for mesoderm formation (Evseenko et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by data and a citation to Evseenko et al., 2010.
